books.section: Topic 1.4 Columbian Exchange, Spanish Exploration, and Conquest
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.text: Wheat, a grain that fed European peasants
options.misconception: Wheat moved westbound, from Europe to the Americas.

options.text: Maize, a crop first grown in Mexico
Horses, which later transformed life on the Great Plains
options.misconception: Horses moved westbound; they were new to the Americas.

options.text: Smallpox, a disease that devastated Native peoples
options.misconception: Smallpox moved westbound, with the colonists.

rationales.general:
1. Play customs officer at the Atlantic. The eastbound column lists what the Americas sent to Europe.
2. Read the crops row. Maize, potatoes, tomatoes, and tobacco moved east.
3. Check the others. Wheat and horses moved west; smallpox moved west too.
4. Match the direction. Only maize among the choices traveled east, so it is the one that fits the table.
Remember: when a question asks which way something moved, read the direction column first.
rationales.B: Maize first grew in Mexico and crossed the Atlantic to Europe after 1492. The table puts it in the eastbound column.
rationales.A: Wheat moved westbound, from Europe to the Americas. It is in the wrong column.
rationales.C: Horses moved westbound. They were new to the Americas, not a crop the Americas sent back.
rationales.D: Smallpox moved westbound, with the colonists. It is in the wrong column.

stem: According to the table, which item moved from the Americas to Europe?

stimulus.source_note: Data table drawn from Barron's Premium 2027 Chapter 3 and 5 Steps to a 5 2024 Chapter 6; the exchange lists are the books' own inventories.
stimulus.text:
| What moved | Westbound (Europe to the Americas) | Eastbound (Americas to Europe) |
| Crops | Wheat, sugarcane | Maize, potatoes, tomatoes, tobacco |
| Animals | Horses, cattle, pigs | The turkey |
| Disease | Smallpox, measles, influenza | None spread widely |
